headline: U.S. Productivity Rose 1.4% as Labor Share Hit a Series Low
dek: Output increased faster than hours worked in the second quarter, while workers' share of nonfarm business income fell to 52.9%.

sources.title: Productivity and Costs, Second Quarter 2026, Preliminary

lead.creator: Shixart1985
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 license granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: A worker operates assembly machinery in a factory. Preliminary BLS data shows nonfarm business productivity increased at a 1.4% annual rate in the second quarter of 2026.
lead.alt: A worker's arm reaches across precision machinery on a factory production line.

charts.caption: Nonfarm business output rose at a 1.7% annual rate while hours worked increased 0.3%, producing a 1.4% productivity gain.
charts.alt: Graphic lists 1.7 percent output growth, 0.3 percent hours growth and 1.4 percent productivity growth.

charts.caption: The labor share of nonfarm business income fell to 52.9%, the lowest in a series beginning in 1947; real hourly compensation fell 3.1% at an annual rate.
charts.alt: Graphic lists a 52.9 percent labor share and a 3.1 percent annualized decline in real hourly compensation.

paragraphs: U.S. nonfarm business labor productivity increased at a 1.4% annual rate in the second quarter of 2026 as output grew faster than hours worked, according to preliminary Bureau of Labor Statistics data.
Output rose 1.7% while hours worked increased 0.3% on seasonally adjusted annual-rate measures. Compared with the second quarter of 2025, productivity was 2.2% higher.

Productivity measures output per hour. It can rise because workers and firms use time, equipment or processes more efficiently, but the quarterly figure does not identify which cause was most important.

Unit labor costs increased 1.3% at an annual rate as hourly compensation grew 2.7%. Unit labor cost is the labor expense required to produce one unit of output, not the same thing as a worker's paycheck.

Inflation-adjusted hourly compensation fell 3.1% at an annual rate during the quarter and was 0.1% lower than a year earlier. Those figures cover the broad nonfarm business sector and do not describe every occupation or household.

Labor's share of nonfarm business income declined to 52.9%, the lowest reading in a series that begins in the first quarter of 1947. The measure compares labor compensation with current-dollar output and can be revised with the underlying national accounts.
Manufacturing productivity increased 1.9% at an annual rate. BLS estimated gains of 2.7% in durable manufacturing and 2.0% in nondurable manufacturing.

Manufacturing unit labor costs were unchanged from the first quarter at an annual rate but stood 3.5% above their year-earlier level. Sector estimates can diverge because output, hours and compensation change at different speeds.
BLS labeled the release preliminary. Revised output, hours and compensation data can change the rates, and annualized quarter-to-quarter movements should not be read as a forecast for the full year.
facts: Nonfarm business productivity rose at a 1.4% annual rate in the second quarter of 2026.
Output rose 1.7% and hours worked rose 0.3%.
Unit labor costs rose 1.3%.
Real hourly compensation fell 3.1% at an annual rate.
Labor share was 52.9%, the lowest in the series beginning in 1947.
uncertainty: The second-quarter figures are preliminary and may be revised.
Annualized aggregate rates do not describe every industry, occupation or household and do not forecast the full year.
seoDescription: BLS says U.S. nonfarm business productivity rose 1.4% in Q2 2026 while labor's income share fell to a series-low 52.9%.

headline: NSF Commits $47 Million to Four-Year Industry-Integrated PhD Pilot
dek: More than 250 doctoral students at nearly three dozen universities are expected to combine academic research with an industry placement.
entities: Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships

sources.title: NSF partners with universities and industry to pilot four-year, industry-integrated Ph.D. model

lead.creator: Clauxz
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 public-domain dedication granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: A university engineering research complex. NSF is launching a four-year doctoral pilot that pairs academic work with industry experience.
lead.alt: A tall modern university research building rises against a blue and clouded sky.

charts.caption: NSF plans $47 million over five years for more than 250 doctoral students across nearly three dozen universities.
charts.alt: Graphic lists 47 million dollars, more than 250 doctoral students and nearly three dozen universities.

charts.caption: Universities fund the first year, NSF supports the remaining years and industry covers at least one year of placement costs.
charts.alt: Graphic summarizes university funding in year one, NSF support in later years and at least one industry-funded placement year.

paragraphs: The U.S. National Science Foundation plans to invest $47 million over five years in a pilot intended to produce industry-integrated science and engineering doctorates in four years.
The initiative is expected to support more than 250 doctoral students at nearly three dozen universities, with private companies participating in placements and research guidance.
Students will be co-advised by academic and industry mentors and complete an industry placement lasting at least one year. NSF says the first cohort is scheduled to begin in fall 2026.

Under the model, a participating university funds the student's first year. NSF provides support for the remaining years, while the industry partner covers costs for at least one year of the placement.

The agency described the pilot as a response to changing career paths for advanced STEM graduates. NSF cited data showing that more than 65% of doctoral recipients with definite commitments in selected science and engineering fields were headed to industry.

A four-year target is shorter than many conventional U.S. doctoral timelines. Reaching it will depend on program design, research scope, advising, student progress and whether academic and industry schedules can be coordinated.

NSF says the structure is meant to preserve rigorous academic research while giving students experience with commercial research settings and workforce needs. The announcement does not replace existing doctoral programs or require all participants to work in industry after graduation.
University and company commitments add resources beyond NSF's appropriation, but the agency announcement does not assign a single combined dollar value to every partner contribution.

The pilot's completion times, placement quality and career outcomes will not be known until cohorts progress through the program. The planned student total and university count may change as awards and partnerships are implemented.
facts: NSF plans a $47 million investment over five years.
The pilot is expected to include more than 250 doctoral students.
Nearly three dozen universities and private industry partners are involved.
Students will have academic and industry co-advisers.
Industry placements will last at least one year.
uncertainty: Four-year completion is a program goal rather than a guaranteed outcome for every student.
Final participation and outcomes can change as university and industry awards are implemented.
seoTitle: NSF launches $47 million four-year PhD pilot
seoDescription: NSF's $47 million pilot will pair more than 250 STEM doctoral students with industry placements in a four-year degree model.

headline: NIH Study Maps a Midlife Shift in the Brain's Immune Cells
dek: A molecular atlas of 40 healthy human hippocampi found microglia declined as inflammatory and peripheral-like immune cells became more prominent from about ages 50 to 75.

sources.title: Brain immunity may undergo major midlife overhaul
Single-cell multi-omic atlas of the aging human hippocampus

lead.creator: Rhoda Baer
lead.rightsBasis: Public-domain work released by the National Cancer Institute and its photographer for unrestricted reuse.
lead.caption: Researchers work at microscopes in a laboratory. An NIH-supported study used single-cell molecular methods to map immune changes in the aging human hippocampus.
lead.alt: Three laboratory researchers work with a microscope and research notes beside a bright window.

charts.caption: Researchers profiled postmortem hippocampal tissue from 40 neurologically healthy donors ages 20 to 95.
charts.alt: Graphic lists 40 hippocampus samples and an age range from 20 to 95 years.

charts.caption: The largest immune-cell shift appeared from roughly ages 50 to 75 as microglia declined and other inflammatory cell types became more prominent.
charts.alt: Graphic highlights ages 50 to 75 and a decline in microglia alongside an increase in other immune cells.

paragraphs: Immune-cell composition in the human hippocampus appears to change sharply during midlife, according to an NIH-supported molecular atlas of neurologically healthy postmortem brain tissue.
Researchers examined hippocampal samples from 40 donors ages 20 to 95. The hippocampus supports learning and memory and is affected early in several age-related brain disorders.

The team combined single-cell gene-expression data with measurements of three-dimensional genome organization and epigenetic regulation. That approach allowed investigators to distinguish cell types and examine how their control systems changed with age.
Resident immune cells called microglia declined most noticeably from roughly ages 50 to 75. During the same period, inflammatory and peripheral-like immune cells became more prominent in the samples.

Researchers also reported deterioration in cells associated with the blood-brain barrier and disruption in genome architecture. These molecular patterns identify associations with aging, not proof that a specific change caused disease.
The tissue came from donors without known neurological disease, which helps describe healthy aging but limits direct conclusions about Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease or other diagnoses.

Postmortem studies provide a detailed snapshot but cannot track the same person's brain through time. Differences among donors, tissue quality and the 40-sample size also constrain how precisely the timing can be generalized.

The investigators say future work should test whether the midlife transition can be modified and whether it helps explain vulnerability to later disease. The current study does not establish a diagnostic test or treatment.
NIH reported support from grants R01AG067153, R01AG082127 and 1U01DA052769. The peer-reviewed findings appeared in Science with DOI 10.1126/science.adt8307.
facts: The study analyzed 40 postmortem hippocampi from donors ages 20 to 95.
Samples came from people considered neurologically healthy.
Microglia declined most noticeably from roughly ages 50 to 75.
Inflammatory and peripheral-like immune cells became more prominent.
The study used single-cell gene-expression, genome-organization and epigenetic data.
uncertainty: The cross-sectional postmortem study shows associations and does not establish that immune changes cause neurological disease.
A 40-donor sample cannot define the exact timing or experience of every aging brain.
seoTitle: NIH study maps midlife brain immune-cell shift
seoDescription: An NIH-supported atlas of 40 healthy hippocampi found a major immune-cell transition from about ages 50 to 75.

headline: NSF Puts $50 Million Into Two AI-Driven Materials Platforms
dek: Teams in Texas and Wisconsin will build national user facilities for autonomous alloy and extreme-environment materials research.

sources.title: NSF stands up 2 Materials Innovation Platforms with $50M investment

lead.creator: National Institute of Standards and Technology
lead.rightsBasis: Photograph created by a U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology employee in official duties and marked public domain.
lead.attribution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
lead.caption: A historic NIST metallurgy laboratory. Two new NSF platforms will give outside researchers access to modern autonomous materials experiments and specialized equipment.
lead.alt: A large historic metallurgy laboratory contains optical instruments, glassware and testing equipment on long benches.

charts.caption: NSF awarded $25 million over six years to each of two national Materials Innovation Platforms, for $50 million total.
charts.alt: Graphic lists two 25 million dollar platform awards over six years and a 50 million dollar total.

charts.caption: The platforms expect dozens of visiting scientists each year and target 10% to 20% of visitors from institutions with lower research spending.
charts.alt: Graphic lists dozens of visiting scientists per year and a 10 to 20 percent participation target for lower-research-spending institutions.

paragraphs: The U.S. National Science Foundation awarded $50 million to establish two national Materials Innovation Platforms centered on autonomous experiments and artificial intelligence.
Texas A&M University and the University of Wisconsin–Madison will each receive $25 million over six years to build facilities open to academic and industry researchers from around the country.

Texas A&M's ARM-MIP will focus on advanced alloys and combine automated synthesis, characterization and AI-guided experimentation. Potential applications include transportation, energy and other systems that require lighter or stronger metals.

Wisconsin's MATRIX-MIP will develop materials designed for extreme heat and radiation. The platform will integrate computation, robotic experiments and specialized testing for environments such as advanced energy systems.
NSF says the facilities will host dozens of visiting scientists annually. The agency expects 10% to 20% of visitors to come from institutions with comparatively low research spending.

National user access is a central condition of the platform model: equipment and staff are not reserved only for the host universities. Actual access will depend on proposal review, capacity, safety and scheduling.
Autonomous experiments can test materials and update models faster than a purely manual sequence, but AI guidance does not eliminate calibration, validation or expert interpretation.

NSF also awarded $4.6 million over four years to help Pennsylvania State University's 2D Crystal Consortium transition after earlier platform support. That amount is separate from the two new $25 million awards.

The six-year awards establish capacity rather than guarantee a specific commercial material or discovery. Research output, outside-user participation and industrial impact will depend on implementation after the facilities come online.
facts: NSF awarded $50 million across two Materials Innovation Platforms.
Texas A&M and Wisconsin will each receive $25 million over six years.
The platforms will use autonomous experiments and AI guidance.
Facilities will be open to national academic and industry users.
NSF expects 10% to 20% of visitors from lower-research-spending institutions.
uncertainty: The awards fund research infrastructure and do not guarantee a specific discovery or commercial product.
User counts and participation shares are implementation targets that can vary with demand and facility capacity.
seoTitle: NSF awards $50 million for AI materials labs
seoDescription: NSF awarded Texas A&M and Wisconsin $25 million each for national, AI-driven materials research platforms.

headline: NOAA Begins 30-Day West Coast Ocean Acidification Survey
dek: The R/V Sikuliaq is measuring chemistry, biology and physics from Southern California to Washington while an uncrewed vessel samples southbound.

sources.title: NOAA scientists set sail for landmark West Coast ocean acidification survey

lead.creator: James Buchanan
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.attribution: James Buchanan / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
lead.caption: The research vessel Sikuliaq at Woods Hole in 2014. The ship departed San Diego for NOAA's 2026 West Coast ocean acidification survey.
lead.alt: The blue-and-white research vessel Sikuliaq sits at a dock under a pale sky.

charts.caption: The 261-foot Sikuliaq is traveling from San Diego toward Washington during a 30-day survey of West Coast waters.
charts.alt: Graphic lists a 30-day survey, a 261-foot ship and a route from San Diego to Washington.

charts.caption: The cruise is collecting ocean chemistry, biology and physics alongside environmental DNA and plankton observations.
charts.alt: Graphic lists chemistry, biology, physics, environmental DNA and plankton measurements.

paragraphs: NOAA scientists departed San Diego aboard the research vessel Sikuliaq for a 30-day survey of ocean acidification and low-oxygen conditions along the U.S. West Coast.
The 261-foot vessel is traveling north toward Washington while researchers measure seawater chemistry, biology and physics across coastal and offshore stations.

The team is collecting environmental DNA and observing phytoplankton and zooplankton in addition to standard carbonate-chemistry measurements. Those data can connect changing seawater conditions with marine ecosystems.

Two days after the ship's departure, an uncrewed SeaTrac vessel was scheduled to begin a southbound route from Washington. NOAA plans to compare its measurements with the ship's observations and other sensors.
The survey occurs during the season when acidification and hypoxia can be most pronounced in West Coast waters. NOAA says a possible El Niño adds another source of variability to the 2026 conditions.

Ocean acidification occurs as seawater absorbs carbon dioxide and its chemistry changes. Lower calcium-carbonate saturation can make shell formation more difficult for oysters and other organisms, but impacts vary by species, life stage and local conditions.
The cruise will help calibrate models and autonomous sensors used by researchers, fishery managers and coastal communities. A single survey cannot by itself define long-term trends.

Shipboard data will require processing and quality control after collection. Preliminary observations can change, and the survey announcement did not report final 2026 acidification or oxygen results.
NOAA characterizes the work as part of a long-running West Coast observing effort. Comparisons across years must account for season, location, upwelling, temperature and large-scale climate patterns.
facts: The Sikuliaq departed San Diego for a 30-day survey.
The research vessel is 261 feet long.
The route extends north toward Washington.
Researchers are collecting chemistry, biology, physics, environmental-DNA and plankton data.
An uncrewed SeaTrac vessel is sampling southbound from Washington.
uncertainty: The cruise announcement precedes final 2026 measurements, which require processing and quality control.
A single seasonal survey cannot establish long-term trends without comparison to other years and observing systems.
seoTitle: NOAA starts 30-day West Coast acidification survey
seoDescription: NOAA's R/V Sikuliaq began a 30-day survey from San Diego to Washington to measure acidification, hypoxia and marine ecosystems.

headline: US Open Offers Oura Rings to Main-Draw Players in Five-Year Deal
dek: The USTA's first wearable partnership includes on-site fitting and education, a coaching recovery module and a planned performance-center recovery area.

sources.title: USTA, US Open announce partnership with Oura as an official sponsor

lead.creator: Nimah Salihu
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.attribution: Nimah Salihu / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
lead.caption: Players compete on an outdoor tennis court in Nigeria. A new USTA partnership will make Oura rings available to every 2026 US Open main-draw player.
lead.alt: Two tennis players move across opposite sides of a blue outdoor court during a rally.

charts.caption: The five-year agreement is the USTA's first wearable partnership and offers a ring to every US Open main-draw player.
charts.alt: Graphic lists a five-year agreement, the USTA's first wearable partnership and availability to all main-draw players.

charts.caption: The arrangement includes on-site fitting and education, a USTA coaching recovery module and a recovery area planned for 2027.
charts.alt: Graphic lists on-site fitting, a coaching recovery module and a 2027 recovery area.

paragraphs: Every main-draw player at the 2026 US Open will be offered an Oura Ring through a new five-year sponsorship agreement between the wearable company and the United States Tennis Association.
The USTA described the arrangement as its first partnership with a wearable-technology company. Players can visit an on-site gifting suite for fitting and education during the tournament.

Oura rings track signals such as sleep, activity, temperature trends and heart rate. The devices provide estimates and wellness indicators; they are not a substitute for clinical diagnosis or individualized medical care.

The deal also adds recovery content to USTA Coaching and USTA League programs. The organizations say the module will focus on sleep, recovery and preparation for tennis participants beyond the professional event.
Oura will become a founding partner of the USTA Player Performance Center and receive naming rights for a recovery area when the center is scheduled to open in 2027.
The USTA said Oura members have recorded 5.5 million hours of tennis activity. That is a company and community-platform count, not an independently audited estimate of all tennis participation.

The association reported 1.14 million attendance at the 2025 US Open and said broadcast coverage reached an estimated audience above 200 million across more than 200 countries. Those figures describe the prior tournament and are provided by the event organizer.

Participation by players is an offer under a sponsorship, not a requirement to wear the ring in competition or share personal data publicly. The announcement does not disclose financial terms or specify every data-governance arrangement.

Wearable readings can be influenced by fit, device algorithms and individual physiology. The partnership establishes access and educational programming, but it does not demonstrate that the device improves match results or prevents injury.
facts: The USTA and Oura announced a five-year partnership.
The USTA calls it the association's first wearable partnership.
A ring will be available to every US Open main-draw player.
On-site fitting and education are planned.
A performance-center recovery area is planned for 2027.
uncertainty: The announcement does not disclose financial terms or every data-governance detail.
Wearable readings are estimates, and the partnership does not establish improved performance or injury prevention.
seoTitle: US Open offers Oura rings to main-draw players
seoDescription: A five-year USTA-Oura deal will offer rings to every 2026 US Open main-draw player and add recovery education to coaching programs.
